decisions.reason: The rejected-clip handling applies to the client's current approval workflow and does not necessarily change the future Lead Clipper responsibilities or pathway.
The existing counting rule already states that only personally approved clips count, so returning a rejected clip until corrected adds no new quota value.
The source decision governs rejected clips in the ongoing monthly production role, not the earlier task-local qualification procedure.
Sending a noncompliant clip back does not change the established project-chat submission channel or submission content.
Publishing remains restricted to client-approved clips; the new rejected-clip correction workflow does not alter that rule or the Instagram destination.
The source establishes what happens after a clip misses the standard but does not modify the moment-selection standard itself.
No caption color, font, or effect rule is changed by the rejected-clip handling decision.
The rejected-clip workflow does not change the existing 30-to-90-second duration requirement.
The source decision does not alter permitted content sources, topic constraints, or the trial batch-source constraint.
The message references overall quality standards but does not modify the clean-editing, effects, or transition rules.
The rejected-clip handling does not change the requirement that each clip contain a complete standalone lesson or story.
